title: Union Minister for Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches AI-Enabled 'Rural Internal Audit Portal' at “Rashtriya Gramin Vikas Sammelan”
text:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau

Ministry of Rural Development

Union Minister for Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches AI-Enabled 'Rural Internal Audit Portal' at “Rashtriya Gramin Vikas Sammelan”

“Rural Internal Audit Portal”: A First-of-its-Kind Unified Digital Platform for End-to-End Management of Internal Audits Covering Both Risk-Based and Compliance Audits

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
28 JUN 2026 2:36PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today launched the 'Rural Internal Audit Portal' during the Rashtriya Gramin Vikas Sammelan at Pusa Campus in New Delhi. The AI-enabled portal marks a significant step towards enhancing transparency, accountability and technology-driven governance in the Ministry of Rural Development.

Recognizing the need to modernize conventional audit practices and leverage emerging digital technologies, the Ministry of Rural Development developed the Rural Internal Audit Portal -a first-of-its-kind unified digital platform for end-to-end management of internal audits covering both risk-based and compliance audits. Conceived by the Office of the Chief Controller of Accounts (CCA), Ministry of Rural Development, and developed in collaboration with the National Informatics Centre (NIC), the Portal represents a significant milestone in the Ministry's digital governance journey.

The Rural Internal Audit Portal has transformed internal audit from a fragmented, paper-intensive and largely manual exercise into a transparent, technology-enabled and data-driven management system. By integrating audit planning, execution, reporting, compliance management, monitoring and analytics within a single digital ecosystem, the Portal has strengthened governance and enhanced the effectiveness of internal audit across Rural Development programmes.

Genesis and Development Journey

The idea of a unified audit management platform emerged from the need to overcome challenges associated with traditional audit processes. Internal audits were often characterized by dispersed records, manual correspondence, delayed reporting, limited monitoring capabilities and inadequate availability of historical audit information for analysis and decision-making. The absence of a centralized repository also made it difficult to track recurring observations, assess systemic risks and monitor compliance over time.

To address these challenges, the Ministry initiated the development of a comprehensive digital solution that would streamline audit processes while promoting transparency, accountability and institutional memory. Extensive consultations were undertaken with auditors, programme divisions, field functionaries and other stakeholders to map existing workflows and identify opportunities for process re-engineering.

A pilot implementation of the Portal was launched in Chandauli District of Uttar Pradesh on 1 April 2025. The successful completion of the pilot validated the platform's capabilities and demonstrated its potential to transform audit administration. Following the pilot phase, the Portal was progressively expanded, and all core modules became operational from October 2025.

Within a short span of implementation, the platform emerged as a comprehensive audit management system capable of supporting the complete audit lifecycle- from audit planning and engagement approvals to audit observations, Action Taken Reports (ATRs), para settlement and archival of records.

Objectives of the Portal

The Rural Internal Audit Portal has been developed with the following objectives:

Digitize and simplify the entire internal audit process to improve efficiency, transparency and accountability. Create a centralized repository of audit units, audit observations, Action Taken Reports and audit records. Enable risk-based audit planning through systematic identification and prioritization of audit units. Automate the generation of audit reports and standardize audit documentation. Leverage analytics and emerging technologies to identify implementation risks and systemic weaknesses. Facilitate real-time monitoring of audit progress, compliance status and approval workflows. Evaluate outputs and outcomes of internal audit interventions. Promote paperless and environmentally sustainable governance practices.

Technology Architecture and Security Framework

The Rural Internal Audit Portal has been developed using a modern, scalable and secure technology architecture aligned with Government of India standards for digital governance.

The platform is hosted and managed with the technical support of the National Informatics Centre (NIC) and incorporates contemporary software engineering practices, including Git-based version control systems and Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) workflows. Separate Development, User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and Production environments ensure controlled deployment of updates and uninterrupted operations.

A comprehensive security framework has been integrated into the Portal architecture. Key elements include role-based access control, centralized monitoring systems, secure API-based integrations, automated exception handling, complete audit logging, periodic security assessments and daily backup mechanisms. Disaster recovery protocols have also been incorporated to ensure business continuity and protection of critical audit data.

The architecture has been designed as a future-ready platform capable of integrating Artificial Intelligence, advanced analytics and machine learning tools for risk assessment, audit prioritization and decision support.

Key Features

The Rural Internal Audit Portal offers a comprehensive suite of functionalities that support every stage of the audit lifecycle.

End-to-End Digital Audit Management

The Portal facilitates complete online management of audit activities, including user registration, audit planning, audit engagement preparation, issuance of audit memoranda, audit observations, report preparation, approvals and record management.

Action Taken Reports and Para Settlement

Auditees can submit Action Taken Reports along with supporting documents through the Portal. Auditors can examine responses, communicate observations and digitally settle audit paras based on compliance achieved.

Centralized Audit Repository

The platform maintains a comprehensive digital repository of audit records, observations, reports and compliance responses. Historical audit information remains readily accessible for future reference, institutional learning and trend analysis.

Role-Based Governance Framework

Dedicated access is provided to auditors, auditees, approving authorities, programme divisions, State Governments, district-level users and certified internal auditors. This ensures secure and structured participation by all stakeholders.

Real-Time Monitoring and Analytics

Interactive dashboards provide real-time information on audit coverage, pending observations, ATR compliance, financial irregularities, audit performance and implementation trends. Decision-makers can access consolidated information at multiple administrative levels.

Geospatial Monitoring through Map View

One of the most innovative features of the Portal is the Map View Module, which provides a geospatial visualization of audit activities across India. The module enables monitoring of audit coverage, deployment of audit teams, para settlement status and compliance responses through an intuitive map-based interface.

Importantly, the module identifies audit units that have never been audited, thereby enabling targeted interventions, optimal deployment of resources and risk-based prioritization of audit activities.

Multilingual and User-Friendly Interface

The Portal has been designed to ensure ease of use and wider accessibility through intuitive workflows, structured navigation and user-friendly interfaces.

Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Analytics

The Ministry is progressively integrating AI-enabled functionalities into the Portal ecosystem. These capabilities are expected to support intelligent audit planning, identification of high-risk entities, predictive analytics, pattern recognition and evidence-based decision-making. The introduction of AI-powered audit assistance represents the next phase in the evolution of digital audit governance within the Ministry.

Impact and Outcomes

The implementation of the Rural Internal Audit Portal has resulted in significant improvements in audit administration and governance outcomes.

The Portal has standardized audit reporting practices and established a uniform framework for managing audit observations across programmes and locations. Audit records are now maintained digitally, ensuring better traceability, accessibility and preservation of institutional knowledge.

Real-time monitoring capabilities have significantly improved oversight and enabled timely interventions. Compliance management has become more transparent through digital tracking of Action Taken Reports and para settlement status.

The platform has reduced dependence on physical records, manual correspondence and fragmented communication channels. Automated workflows have accelerated approvals, minimized procedural delays and improved coordination among stakeholders.

The availability of analytical dashboards has enhanced the Ministry's ability to identify trends, assess risks and monitor implementation quality. As a result, internal audit has evolved from a compliance-focused exercise into a strategic management tool supporting programme effectiveness and governance reforms.

National Recognition and Adoption

The success of the Rural Internal Audit Portal has attracted recognition at the national level as a model digital governance initiative.

In acknowledgement of its transformative potential, the Office of the Controller General of Accounts (CGA), Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure, issued Office Memorandum No. I-104/3/2024-ITD-CGA/E-19878/621A dated 09 December 2025 conveying in-principle approval for implementation of the Internal Audit Module of the Ministry of Rural Development across all Principal Chief Controller of Accounts (Pr. CCA), Chief Controller of Accounts (CCA) and Controller of Accounts (CA) offices of Civil Ministries and Departments.

The Office Memorandum recognized the Rural Internal Audit Portal as the first unified digital platform for end-to-end management of internal audits covering both risk-based and compliance audits. It highlighted the Portal's capabilities in audit planning, engagement approvals, audit memoranda, real-time management of observations, para-wise financial tracking, audit report generation and digital processing of Action Taken Reports.

This recognition marks an important milestone in the evolution of digital public financial management in India and positions the Rural Internal Audit Portal as a benchmark platform for strengthening internal audit governance across Government.

The Road Ahead

The Ministry of Rural Development envisions the Rural Internal Audit Portal as a continuously evolving platform that will increasingly leverage emerging technologies to strengthen governance and accountability.

Future enhancements include deeper integration of Artificial Intelligence, advanced risk-scoring mechanisms, predictive analytics, intelligent audit planning tools and enhanced management dashboards. These innovations will further improve the quality, efficiency and strategic relevance of internal audits while supporting evidence-based governance.
